newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK mulls investor access to stock clearing system.
newsitem.headline: HK mulls investor access to stock clearing system.

text.p: Hong Kong Securities Clearing Co Ltd presented a proposal on Thursday to open its Central Clearing and Settlement System (CCASS) for listed securities to individual and corporate investors.
Under the working model, investors would be allowed to open stock accounts directly in CCASS, which would in effect be depository accounts for share custody.

Currently only brokers, custodians and other intermediaries through whom investors deal can participate in CCASS, while investors can hold physical shares, ask an intermediary to open a segregated CCASS account or entrust shares to an intermediary.
Under the proposal, investors would benefit from computerised book-entry settlement, avoiding the risk of losing share certificates and eliminating the cost of registration of share transfers.

They would have full control over the movement of shares in the CCASS depository and have better legal protection in case of insolvency of brokers or custodians, and would get direct distribution of corporate information and announcements.

But investors would have to undertake to make timely affirmations of deals and instructions on corporate actions, as well as pay various fees and a monthly subscription, which will depend on the level of participation, Hongkong Clearing said.

Hongkong Clearing said it would conduct a three-month public consultation on the proposal, first querying CCASS participants, listed companies and other market practitioners, then surveying investors.
Hongkong Clearing is a non-profit distribution company engaged in developing and operating a central clearing and settlement system for listed securities in Hong Kong.
